comment: The component criteria can be interpreted as a one-component/one-product procurement blueprint. This misrepresents platform architectures. A single DHIS2 deployment can co-realise aggregate HMIS, case/event surveillance, registries, facility profiles, campaigns, community information, analytics and feedback; conversely, one logical capability may be distributed across systems. Mandatory product separation would recreate silos and duplicate metadata, hosting, support and user workflows.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

public.text: The component criteria can be interpreted as a one-component/one-product procurement blueprint. This misrepresents platform architectures. A single DHIS2 deployment can co-realise aggregate HMIS, case/event surveillance, registries, facility profiles, campaigns, community information, analytics and feedback; conversely, one logical capability may be distributed across systems. Mandatory product separation would recreate silos and duplicate metadata, hosting, support and user workflows.
public.suggestedRevision: State prominently that components are logical capabilities, not mandatory software, procurement or deployment boundaries. Permit one governed platform to implement several components and one component to be distributed across services. Conformance should test capabilities, interfaces, safeguards and outcomes rather than count products or boxes.
